documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Reviewed December pulm note with him - lung function lower, same inhalers. He says the winter was 'about like last winter.' Rescue inhaler most days now. No infections, no hospital.

Legs unchanged. Eyes: uses the Amsler grid, no new distortion; eye doctor visits every six months.

Vitals per flowsheet, weight steady. Lungs: diminished, prolonged expiration, scattered wheeze. Heart regular. No edema.

- COPD: continue tiotropium/albuterol.
- HTN: BMP today.
- Colon screening: 10 years since the normal colonoscopy. He doesn't want another scope; FIT kit given with instructions.
- Tobacco: still 1 ppd, quitting discussed, not ready.
Physical in June.

documents.title: Annual visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual + problem visit.

Following COPD, PAD with claudication and tobacco use. He feels okay but his belt is looser - down about 10 lb over roughly three months without trying. Eating 'like always.' No fevers, no night sweats, no blood when he coughs; morning cough no different from the last few years.

Weight 84.6 kg (was in the high 80s in March). BP 132/84, HR 78, RR 16, afebrile.
Gen: thinner in the face. No palpable cervical or supraclavicular nodes. Lungs clear to auscultation today, no wheeze. Heart regular. Abd soft, no masses, no hepatomegaly. Ext no edema.

CXR done in the office this morning (no older films to compare): 1.2 cm spiculated nodule in the RUL.

A/P
1. Unintentional weight loss with a spiculated RUL nodule in a 40 pk-yr current smoker - concerning for lung cancer until shown otherwise. CT chest ordered for this week. CBC, CMP, TSH today. Discussed with him plainly; he took it quietly.
2. COPD/HTN/PAD - unchanged regimen.
3. Prevention - FIT negative March. PHQ-2 0.

conditions.label: Solitary pulmonary nodule, high suspicion for malignancy

reports.text:
CT CHEST WITHOUT CONTRAST
Indication: RUL nodule on chest radiograph, weight loss, smoker.
Comparison: chest radiograph 6/9/2025. No prior CT.
Findings: Solitary 1.2 cm nodule in the right upper lobe with spiculated margins. No additional pulmonary nodules. No mediastinal, hilar or axillary lymphadenopathy. No pleural or pericardial effusion. Heart size normal. Upper abdomen unremarkable. Osseous structures intact.
reports.conclusion: Solitary 1.2 cm spiculated right upper lobe nodule, highly suspicious for primary lung malignancy. No additional abnormality. Tissue sampling and PET-CT recommended.

documents.title: CT chest - flagged
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CT confirms the single spiculated 1.2 cm RUL nodule, nothing else. Will call him Monday with results and the plan for PET + biopsy via pulmonology.

orders.reason: spiculated RUL nodule, high suspicion for malignancy; PET-CT and tissue diagnosis

documents.title: CT result call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt with CT results. Explained the nodule looks suspicious for cancer and the next steps are a PET scan and a biopsy through the lung doctors he already knows. Urgent referral sent; their office will call to book. He asked if it could be 'just scar from the smoking' - told him that's possible but unlikely with this appearance and we shouldn't wait. He agreed to the referral.

documents.title: Pulmonology appointment notice

documents.body: Notice to referring provider: patient cancelled new-problem appointment scheduled 7/7/2025 (nodule evaluation). Did not reschedule at time of call. Referral remains open in our system.

documents.title: Call re: cancelled pulmonology visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reached him at home after the pulm office let us know he cancelled. He says he feels fine and wants to 'get through the summer' before any more scans or needles. Went over again why the nodule worries me and that waiting can let it spread. He heard it, still wants to wait. He knows the referral stays open and he can call them directly. Asked him to let me know if anything changes - cough, blood, more weight loss, anything. Will touch base in the fall.

documents.title: Office visit - weakness
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: legs weak.

HPI: Since roughly the start of October (about 7 weeks) stairs have become hard and he has to push up with his arms to get out of a chair. Mouth is dry all the time. Every so often sees double, usually later in the day; resting his eyes clears it. Bowel and bladder normal. No numbness. No new cough or hemoptysis. Weight drifting down.

He has not gone back to pulmonology about the nodule.

Exam: Weight 82.1 kg. Other vitals per flowsheet. Alert, thin. EOM full without diplopia at rest in the room. Hip flexors and shoulder abductors 4/5 both sides; distal strength full. Reflexes hypoactive and symmetric at knees and biceps. Sensation intact. Gait slow, can't rise from chair without arms. Lungs diminished, prolonged expiration. Heart regular.

A/P: Subacute proximal weakness, dry mouth and fatigable diplopia in a smoker with a suspicious lung nodule - I'm worried about a paraneoplastic neuromuscular syndrome (Lambert-Eaton) or other neuromuscular junction disease. BMP, CBC, CK, TSH today. Urgent neurology referral. Re-referred to pulmonology marked expedited; this time he says yes and wants to know what's going on. Fall precautions discussed. Call for trouble swallowing or breathing.

documents.title: Blood tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Joseph, the blood work from Tuesday was normal - muscle enzyme, thyroid, salts and blood counts. That doesn't explain the weakness, so the neurology visit is still important. They have you on December 22. Pulmonology should call this week.

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Comparison: chest radiograph 6/9/2025 (outside report). There is a right hilar mass. The lungs are hyperexpanded. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal.
reports.conclusion: Right hilar mass. Further evaluation with CT/PET recommended.

documents.title: Neurology consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 12/22/2025 (transcribed and sent 1/21/2026)

Referral: proximal weakness.

HPI: 70-year-old man, 40 pack-year smoker, COPD, peripheral arterial disease and macular degeneration, with a right upper lobe nodule found in June that has been concerning for cancer but not yet sampled. Over three months he has had increasing trouble with stairs and standing from a chair. Dry mouth. Intermittent double vision that gets better with rest. No bowel or bladder symptoms.

Meds: lisinopril 20, HCTZ 12.5, atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81, tiotropium, albuterol.
NKDA.

Exam: Weakness of proximal muscles, symmetric, arms and legs. Deep tendon reflexes reduced; they become brisker after 10 seconds of maximal contraction. Sensation normal. Cranial nerves intact at the time of exam.

Data: BMP and CBC from primary care normal. Chest radiograph today shows a right hilar mass.

Impression: Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome, very likely paraneoplastic given the lung findings; small cell lung cancer is the leading concern.

Plan:
- EMG/NCS with repetitive stimulation and P/Q-type VGCC antibody (done 12/30 - see addendum).
- Urgent PET-CT and tissue diagnosis; pulmonology contacted directly.
- Symptomatic treatment once electrodiagnostics confirm.

ADDENDUM 1/5/2026: EMG/RNS findings typical of a presynaptic disorder (report attached). P/Q-type VGCC antibody 0.41 nmol/L, positive. Started amifampridine 10 mg three times daily. Follow-up in neurology clinic in 6-8 weeks.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth three times daily

reports.text:
Motor nerve conductions (median, ulnar, peroneal, tibial): compound muscle action potential amplitudes low in all nerves tested (ulnar to abductor digiti minimi 1.9 mV); distal latencies and conduction velocities normal. Sensory responses normal.
Repetitive nerve stimulation, ulnar at 3 Hz: 24% decrement.
After 10 seconds of maximal voluntary exercise: CMAP amplitude increment of 210%.
Needle EMG of proximal and distal muscles: no fibrillations; no myopathic units.
reports.conclusion: Presynaptic neuromuscular junction disorder, consistent with Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome.

documents.title: EMG/NCS report
documents.author: neurology
documents.body: Electrodiagnostic study 12/30/2025, outside neurology lab. Full report attached to consultation of 12/22/2025. Low-amplitude CMAPs with 3 Hz decrement and marked post-exercise facilitation (210%); normal sensory studies; no myopathic changes. Interpretation: presynaptic NMJ disorder, consistent with LEMS.

He says the nerve test 'showed the signal isn't getting through' and the neurologist wants him on a pill three times a day; first fill came yesterday. PET scan is this Friday, brain MRI Monday, lung doctor doing a biopsy the following week. Sounds tired but clear. Booked visit with PCP 1/27.

reports.text:
FDG PET-CT, skull base to mid-thigh.
Comparison: CT chest 6/13/2025.
The right upper lobe nodule now measures 1.9 cm, SUV max 8.6.
Right hilar (station 10R) nodal mass 3.1 cm, SUV max 11.4.
Right lower paratracheal (4R) node 1.5 cm, SUV max 6.2.
No other hypermetabolic thoracic nodes. No hypermetabolic lesion in the liver, adrenal glands or skeleton. Physiologic uptake elsewhere.
reports.conclusion: Enlarging hypermetabolic right upper lobe nodule with hypermetabolic right hilar and right lower paratracheal nodes. No distant hypermetabolic disease.

conditions.label: Solitary pulmonary nodule, high suspicion for malignancy
Small cell carcinoma of right upper lobe of lung
conditions.note: limited stage, cT1b N2 M0, stage IIIA

reports.text:
Specimens: A) Lymph node, station 10R, EBUS-TBNA. B) Lymph node, station 4R, EBUS-TBNA. C) Lymph node, station 7, EBUS-TBNA.
A and B: Small cell carcinoma. Tumor cells with scant cytoplasm, finely granular chromatin and nuclear molding; abundant mitoses and crush artifact. Immunostains: synaptophysin positive, TTF-1 positive. Ki-67 approximately 85%.
C: Benign lymphoid tissue, negative for malignancy.
reports.conclusion: Small cell carcinoma involving stations 10R and 4R. Station 7 negative.

documents.title: EBUS-TBNA
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE INTERVENTIONAL PULMONOLOGY
Procedure date: 1/16/2026
Procedure: Flexible bronchoscopy with endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration.
Indication: RUL nodule with PET-avid right hilar and paratracheal nodes; Lambert-Eaton syndrome.
Anesthesia: moderate sedation. Airway inspection: no endobronchial lesion.
Nodes sampled: 10R (4 passes), 4R (3 passes), 7 (3 passes). Rapid on-site evaluation: malignant cells at 10R and 4R.
No complications; discharged home same day.
Final pathology (1/20): small cell carcinoma at 10R and 4R; station 7 negative.
Impression: Small cell lung cancer, right upper lobe primary, limited stage (cT1b N2 M0). Referred to thoracic oncology.

documents.title: Neurology and pathology reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Neurology consult from 12/22 finally here, with EMG and antibody: LEMS confirmed, VGCC Ab positive, on amifampridine. EBUS path: small cell at 10R and 4R. Seeing him 1/27; oncology is 1/29.

documents.title: Office visit - new diagnosis
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to go over everything from the last month.

Summary of outside work-up:
- Neuro 12/22: LEMS; EMG 12/30 with 210% post-exercise increment; P/Q VGCC Ab 0.41, positive. Amifampridine 10 mg TID since early January.
- PET 1/9: RUL 1.9 cm, hot 10R and 4R nodes, no distant disease. Brain MRI 1/12 clear.
- EBUS 1/16: small cell carcinoma at 10R and 4R.

He says the new pill has helped - he can get off the couch without rocking now, stairs still slow. Double vision less often. Mouth still dry. Eating less, weight 80.3 kg. Breathing his usual.

Exam: thin, alert. Proximal strength 4+/5 hips. Lungs diminished, prolonged expiration. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P
1. Small cell lung cancer, RUL, limited stage (cT1b N2 M0) - added to list, nodule entry closed. Oncology consult Thursday. He knows this is a serious cancer and that limited-stage disease is treated with the aim of cure.
2. LEMS, paraneoplastic - added; amifampridine on med list. Neurology following.
3. Advance care planning (~25 min): he wants full treatment, full code. Health care proxy form given; he'll bring it back signed.
4. Weight loss - nutrition basics, add a shake between meals.
5. COPD/HTN/PAD - unchanged.
6. Tobacco - still smoking. Offered patch again; he wants to try on his own first.

medications.sig: Dissolve 1 tablet on the tongue every 8 hours as needed for nausea

documents.title: Thoracic oncology consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE THORACIC ONCOLOGY - MULTIDISCIPLINARY CONSULT
Seen 1/29/2026 by medical and radiation oncology.

Diagnosis: Small cell lung cancer, right upper lobe, with ipsilateral hilar (10R) and paratracheal (4R) nodal involvement; station 7 negative. PET without distant disease; brain MRI negative. Limited stage, cT1b N2 M0 (stage IIIA). Paraneoplastic Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome, VGCC antibody positive, on amifampridine per neurology.

Comorbidities: COPD (FEV1 1.0 L, 40% predicted, 12/2024), PAD with claudication, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, dry AMD. Current smoker, 40 pack-years.

Meds: lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, atorvastatin, aspirin, tiotropium, albuterol, amifampridine 10 mg TID. NKDA.

Recommendation (discussed with patient, who wishes to proceed):
1. Carboplatin AUC 5 day 1 plus etoposide 100 mg/m2 days 1-3, every 21 days for 4 cycles.
2. Concurrent thoracic radiation, 60 Gy in 30 once-daily fractions, starting with or shortly after cycle 1 (once daily chosen given lung function).
3. Durvalumab consolidation after chemoradiation if no progression.
4. Brain MRI surveillance every 3 months rather than prophylactic cranial irradiation.
5. Ondansetron 4 mg ODT every 8 hours as needed for nausea; antiemetic premedication in the infusion center.
6. Smoking cessation strongly encouraged.

Cycle 1 planned 2/2/2026.

medications.sig: AUC 5 IV on day 1 every 21 days for 4 cycles
100 mg/m2 IV on days 1-3 every 21 days for 4 cycles

Outside oncology infusion note (copy to PCP).
C1D1 carboplatin AUC 5 / etoposide 100 mg/m2. Labs adequate for treatment. Premedicated. Tolerated without reaction. Returns days 2 and 3 for etoposide. Radiation simulation done; RT to begin 2/9. Next cycle 2/23.

documents.title: Check-in call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Outreach call during treatment. He's had two of four chemo cycles and is about four weeks into radiation, 'tired but standing.' Taking his regular pills. Has the nausea tabs, used a few. No fevers. Ride program from oncology getting him to daily radiation. Asked us to keep his refills going - all on auto-refill at mail order.

documents.title: Radiation treatment summary
documents.author: radiation oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE RADIATION ONCOLOGY - END OF TREATMENT SUMMARY
Diagnosis: limited-stage small cell lung cancer, RUL, N2.
Treatment: 60 Gy in 30 once-daily fractions to the right upper lobe primary and involved 10R/4R nodes, 2/9/2026 - 3/20/2026, concurrent with carboplatin/etoposide.
Completed as planned without breaks. Acute effects: fatigue.
Follow-up: radiation oncology in 6 weeks; restaging CT per medical oncology after cycle 4.

documents.title: Video visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit from his kitchen, identity confirmed by DOB.

Finished radiation 3/20 and the fourth chemo cycle 4/6. Tired, naps in the afternoon. Eating better, using the shakes. Legs noticeably stronger - climbed his porch steps without the railing last week. Double vision hasn't come back. Mouth still a bit dry. Breathing his usual; albuterol some days. Still smoking.

Visual exam limited: looks thin but well, speaking full sentences, no work of breathing on camera.

A/P: SCLC s/p chemoradiation - restaging CT early May per oncology; durvalumab to follow if no progression. LEMS improving on amifampridine. COPD stable. Continue all meds. In-person visit this summer.

reports.text:
CT CHEST WITH CONTRAST
Comparison: PET-CT 1/9/2026.
Right upper lobe primary now 0.8 cm (previously 1.9 cm). Right hilar 10R node 1.1 cm (previously 3.1 cm). Right lower paratracheal 4R node 0.9 cm (previously 1.5 cm). Post-radiation change in the right paramediastinal lung. No new nodules. No pleural effusion. No new lymphadenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen without lesion.
reports.conclusion: Partial response of the right upper lobe primary and right hilar and paratracheal nodes after chemoradiation. Expected post-radiation change. No new disease.

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First in-person visit since January.

Oncology update per pt (we did not get notes): restaging CT in May showed the tumor and nodes shrinking; started durvalumab infusions mid-May, every four weeks, third one was last week. No rash, no diarrhea, no cough beyond his usual. Brain MRI in June clear - report is in our chart. He's walking to the end of his road again; stairs fine. Double vision gone. Still on amifampridine three times a day. Still smoking, though he says less.

Weight 78.8 kg, holding. Other vitals per flowsheet.
Exam: thin, more color than in winter. Lungs diminished, prolonged expiration, no crackles. Heart regular. Hip flexors 5-/5. Skin without rash. Feet cool, faint pulses, intact.

A/P
1. SCLC, limited stage - partial response after chemoradiation, on durvalumab consolidation. Added durvalumab to med list. Requested oncology notes.
2. LEMS - much improved. Continue amifampridine per neurology.
3. COPD - stable, continue tiotropium/albuterol.
4. HTN, PAD - unchanged.
5. Tobacco - still smoking; encouraged to quit, patch offered again, declined.
6. CMP, CBC with diff, TSH today (on immunotherapy).
Follow-up in the fall.

reports.conclusion: Stable treated disease. No new disease.

documents.title: Oncology follow-up
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE THORACIC ONCOLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 8/11/2026 (received 8/19, in response to records request)

On durvalumab 1500 mg every 4 weeks since 5/18/2026, cycle 4 today. No immune-related adverse effects. Surveillance CT 8/10 stable, no new disease. Brain MRI 6/29 negative. LEMS improved on amifampridine. Plan: continue durvalumab; CT every 3 months; brain MRI every 3 months. Next visit with cycle 5.

Included for prior dates: infusion records for carboplatin/etoposide cycles 2-4 (2/23, 3/16, 4/6/2026), completed without dose delays.

Scanned to chart. Lists not updated; for review at next visit.

documents.title: Flu shot this year
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Can I still get the flu shot with the infusions or should I skip it this year?

documents.title: RE: Flu shot this year
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Yes, you should still get it - the flu shot is safe with durvalumab and especially important for you this year. Once this season's vaccine arrives in September you can get it here or at your pharmacy. Your oncology team agrees.
